results.name: outside_minus_inside_range
results.description: Among non-example targets, yes rate for targets outside the [min, max] range of the examples minus targets inside that range; observed above null means people extend beyond the example range more than the model's interval hypotheses allow, below null means they confine generalization to the range more.
results.code:
# name: outside_minus_inside_range
# description: Among non-example targets, yes rate for targets outside the [min, max] range of the examples minus targets inside that range; observed above null means people extend beyond the example range more than the model's interval hypotheses allow, below null means they confine generalization to the range more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    lo = ex.min(axis=1); hi = ex.max(axis=1)
    inside = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    return m((~inset) & (~inside)) - m((~inset) & inside)

results.name: intermediate_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells whose mean yes rate lies in [0.25, 0.75]; observed above null means people's endorsements are more graded/uncertain than the model's posterior predicts, below null means more all-or-none.

results.name: last_digit_match_contrast
results.description: Among non-example targets, yes rate when the target's last digit matches the last digit of some example minus when it matches none; observed below null means the model over-weights ends-in-digit rules relative to people.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_match_contrast
# description: Among non-example targets, yes rate when the target's last digit matches the last digit of some example minus when it matches none; observed below null means the model over-weights ends-in-digit rules relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    match = (ex % 10).eq(t % 10, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    return m((~inset) & match) - m((~inset) & (~match))

results.name: in_set_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed below null means the model over-endorses example members (people reject listed examples more than the model's near-certain membership allows).

results.name: recency_last_vs_first_example
results.description: Among non-example targets in multi-example sets, yes rate when the target is strictly closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown minus the reverse; the model is order-blind, so observed above null means a recency bias, below null a primacy bias.
results.code:
# name: recency_last_vs_first_example
# description: Among non-example targets in multi-example sets, yes rate when the target is strictly closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown minus the reverse; the model is order-blind, so observed above null means a recency bias, below null a primacy bias.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    arr = ex.to_numpy()
    first = arr[:, 0]
    last = arr[np.arange(len(arr)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]
    tv = t.to_numpy()
    df_ = np.abs(tv - first); dl = np.abs(tv - last)
    base = (~inset).to_numpy() & (n >= 2)
    return m(pd.Series(base & (dl < df_), index=df.index)) - m(pd.Series(base & (df_ < dl), index=df.index))

results.name: even_set_parity_contrast
results.description: For sets whose examples are all even, yes rate for even targets minus odd targets (non-example targets); observed above null means people rely on parity more than the model predicts, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: even_set_parity_contrast
# description: For sets whose examples are all even, yes rate for even targets minus odd targets (non-example targets); observed above null means people rely on parity more than the model predicts, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    alleven = ((ex % 2 == 0) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1)
    return m(alleven & (~inset) & (t % 2 == 0)) - m(alleven & (~inset) & (t % 2 == 1))

results.name: proximity_near_minus_far
results.description: Among non-example targets, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed above null means people show stronger graded numeric-similarity generalization than the model, below null means weaker.
results.code:
# name: proximity_near_minus_far
# description: Among non-example targets, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed above null means people show stronger graded numeric-similarity generalization than the model, below null means weaker.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    dist = ex.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    return m((~inset) & (dist <= 3)) - m((~inset) & (dist > 20))

results.name: set_size_four_minus_two
results.description: Overall yes rate on 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means people tighten generalization with more examples less than the (tempered) size principle predicts, below null means more.
results.code:
# name: set_size_four_minus_two
# description: Overall yes rate on 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means people tighten generalization with more examples less than the (tempered) size principle predicts, below null means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    return m(n == 4) - m(n == 2)
